C2-1-0.point: Aspect and nuance: perfect and continuous forms
C2-1-0.title: Perfect result vs continuous activity

examples.t: I’ve been revising all week, so I’m exhausted.
I’ve finished the report; it’s on your desk.

C2-1-0.note_es: El perfecto mira el resultado desde ahora; el continuo destaca la actividad en curso, su duración o su efecto.

C2-1-1.point: Past tenses for distancing and politeness
C2-1-1.title: How indirect is the request?

marks.ex: I wonder if you could help me.
I wondered if you could help me.
I was wondering if you might lend me a hand.

C2-1-1.note_es: El pasado no habla del pasado: pone distancia. El pasado simple suaviza la petición y el pasado continuo es la forma más tentativa.

C2-1-2.title: State vs action meaning

items.t: She has a flat in Rome.

columns.head: dynamic (continuous)
columns.use_es: Describe lo que ocurre o cómo se comporta.

C2-1-2.note_es: Los verbos de estado en continuo cambian de sentido: think = opinar o reflexionar; have = poseer o tomar; be + -ing = comportarse.

C2-2-0.title: It-cleft
C2-2-0.note_es: It + be + elemento destacado + who/that + resto. Sirve para corregir o contrastar: fue Maria, no otra persona.

C2-2-0.title: Wh-cleft with all
C2-2-0.note_es: All (o What) + oración + be + elemento destacado. All I need is… destaca lo único que se necesita; el foco queda al final.

C2-2-1.title: Place fronting with inversion
C2-2-1.note_es: El lugar pasa al inicio y el verbo va antes del sujeto: crea un efecto narrativo o dramático.

C2-2-1.title: Such was… that…
C2-2-1.note_es: El complemento va primero y la oración se invierte para enfatizar el grado.

C2-2-2.point: Inversion after negative and restrictive adverbials
C2-2-2.title: Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject
C2-2-2.note_es: Tras Never, Not only o No sooner al inicio, el auxiliar va antes del sujeto, como en una pregunta.

C2-3-0.point: Modals of speculation and deduction (present, past, future)
C2-3-0.title: Graded certainty

marks.ex: That can’t be Sam; he’s abroad.
It might be a fault in the wiring.
It may well be the best option.
She must be exhausted by now.

C2-3-0.note_es: Con la misma estructura (modal + be, have been, be + -ing) gradúas lo seguro que estás sobre el presente, el pasado o el futuro.

C2-3-1.point: Needn’t have vs didn’t need to; should have, might have, could have
C2-3-1.title: Judging the past

columns.head: didn’t need to
columns.use_es: No dice si se hizo o no.

items.t: I didn’t need to bring food.
We could have won the match.

C2-3-1.note_es: Needn’t have: lo hiciste y no era necesario. Didn’t need to: no era necesario (quizá no lo hiciste). Should/could have: reproche o posibilidad perdida.

C2-3-2.point: Will and would for assumption and characteristic behaviour
C2-3-2.title: Assumption and typical behaviour

columns.head: will
columns.use_es: Presente: lo que supones o sueles hacer.

items.t: That’ll be Sam at the door.

columns.head: would
columns.use_es: Hábito pasado o suposición sobre el pasado.

items.t: Every summer we would visit her.
He would say that, wouldn’t he?

C2-3-2.note_es: Will expresa una suposición o conducta típica ahora; would, lo mismo en el pasado o un comentario sobre alguien predecible.

C2-4-0.title: Verb phrase to noun phrase
C2-4-0.note_es: El verbo pasa a nombre y el adverbio a adjetivo. El resultado es más denso y académico.

C2-4-0.title: Clause to noun phrase as subject
C2-4-0.note_es: Dos oraciones se condensan en una: la acción nominalizada se convierte en sujeto del verbo principal.

C2-4-1.title: Passive: -ed
C2-4-1.note_es: That + be + participio se reduce al participio pasado.

C2-4-1.title: After first, last, only: to-infinitive
C2-4-1.note_es: Tras first, last, only o un superlativo, la relativa se reduce a to + infinitivo.

C2-4-2.point: Advanced verb patterns: gerund vs infinitive with change of meaning
C2-4-2.title: Gerund vs infinitive: new meaning

items.t: She went on talking for an hour.
He proposed to move the meeting.
She went on to become a judge.

C2-4-2.note_es: Mean, propose, go on, regret o stop cambian de sentido: -ing expresa hecho o consecuencia; to + verbo, intención o paso nuevo.

C2-5-0.point: Advanced passives: reporting passives and passive infinitives
C2-5-0.title: Reporting passive with perfect infinitive
C2-5-0.note_es: Si la acción es anterior al verbo de opinión, se usa to have + participio: is thought to have been tested.

C2-5-0.point: Advanced passives: reporting passives and passive infinitives
C2-5-0.title: Reporting passive: said to have
C2-5-0.note_es: Estructura típica de prensa y textos formales: da la información con distancia.

C2-5-1.point: Causatives: have/get something done; have someone do
C2-5-1.title: Three causative patterns

columns.head: have / get + thing + pp
columns.use_es: Otro lo hace por ti, o te ocurre.

items.t: I’ll have the team send it.
She had us rewrite the plan.

C2-5-1.note_es: Have/get + objeto + participio: la acción la hace otro. Have + persona + verbo base; get + persona + to + verbo.

C2-5-2.point: Hedging and impersonal structures in academic English
C2-5-2.title: How strongly do you claim it?

marks.ex: The data may suggest a link.
It would appear that demand is falling.
The study clearly shows a decline.
This proves the theory is correct.

C2-5-2.note_es: Cubrirse bien no es ser débil: gradúa la fuerza de tu afirmación según la evidencia que tengas.

C2-6-0.title: Mixed and implied conditionals

items.t: If I had taken the job, I’d be rich now.
If she weren’t so careful, she’d have failed.
Without your help, I would have failed.
A better driver would have braked.

C2-6-0.note_es: En los mixtos, la condición y el resultado están en tiempos distintos. En los implícitos, la condición se sugiere sin if.

C2-6-1.title: Had + subject + participle
C2-6-1.note_es: Had + sujeto + participio, sin if: condición pasada irreal, muy formal.

C2-6-1.title: Were it not for
C2-6-1.note_es: Were it not for + nombre = si no fuera por. Es la forma invertida y formal de if it were not for.

C2-6-1.title: Should + subject + verb
C2-6-1.note_es: Should + sujeto + verbo base: posibilidad remota, típica de cartas y avisos formales.

C2-6-2.point: Alternatives to if: but for, otherwise, provided, supposing, were it not for
C2-6-2.title: Connectors that replace if

columns.head: but for / were it not for

items.t: But for your help, we’d have failed.
Were it not for him, I’d resign.
Leave now; otherwise, you’ll miss it.

C2-6-2.note_es: Cada conector precisa el tipo de condición: but for = sin; otherwise = o si no; provided = solo si; supposing = hipótesis.

C2-7-0.point: Ellipsis and substitution (so, not, do so, one)
C2-7-0.title: Substitution with so
C2-7-0.note_es: So (o not) sustituye a toda la cláusula tras hope, think, believe y suppose.

C2-7-0.point: Ellipsis and substitution (so, not, do so, one)
C2-7-0.title: Substitution with one
C2-7-0.note_es: One evita repetir un nombre contable ya mencionado.

C2-7-1.point: Intensifiers, downtoners and gradable vs ungradable adjectives
C2-7-1.title: Match the modifier to the adjective
C2-7-1.note_es: Los adjetivos graduables aceptan very o rather. Los extremos o absolutos piden absolutely, utterly o completely.

C2-7-2.title: Order and compound modifiers
C2-7-2.note_es: La opinión va antes que los datos objetivos. Los modificadores compuestos llevan guion cuando van antes del nombre.

C2-8-0.title: Subjunctive and fixed phrases
C2-8-0.note_es: Tras demandas y recomendaciones, el verbo va en forma base. Frases como come what may o be that as it may conservan el subjuntivo.

C2-8-1.point: Unreal past: wish, if only, it’s (high) time, would rather, as if
C2-8-1.title: Unreal past forms

items.t: He acts as if he had won.

C2-8-1.note_es: Un pasado simple expresa algo irreal ahora; un past perfect expresa un pesar sobre el pasado.

C2-8-2.point: Concession and contrast: albeit, notwithstanding, much as, however + adjective
C2-8-2.title: Formal concession

items.t: Much as I admire her, I disagree.
However hard you try, you can’t please everyone.

C2-8-2.note_es: Se concede un punto con elegancia antes de defender el tuyo: albeit y notwithstanding son formales; much as e however + adjetivo dan énfasis.

C2-9-0.point: Future forms in the past (was to, was about to, would)
C2-9-0.title: Looking forward from the past

examples.t: She was about to leave when the phone rang.
The meeting was to start at nine.
He would later become a famous director.

C2-9-0.note_es: Desde un momento del pasado se mira hacia delante: was to (plan), was about to (inminente) y would (lo que ocurriría después).

C2-9-1.point: Discourse markers and cohesive devices at C2
C2-9-1.title: Building an argument

steps.ex: To begin with, the cost is too high.
Moreover, the plan lacks public support.
Consequently, the council delayed the vote.
In sum, the proposal needs revision.

C2-9-1.note_es: Cada conector dice al lector qué hace la frase: abrir, añadir, contrastar, sacar una consecuencia o resumir.

C2-9-2.point: Prepositional and phrasal verb nuance in formal writing
C2-9-2.title: Phrasal verbs in formal writing
C2-9-2.note_es: No todo phrasal verb es informal: carry out o rule out son estándar en textos formales. Otros, como mess up, suenan coloquiales.

C2-10-0.point: Advanced future forms: future perfect continuous, be to, be on the verge of, be due to
C2-10-0.title: Advanced future forms

examples.t: By next June, I’ll have been working here for ten years.
The train is due to arrive at six.
The president is to visit Rome next week.
She is on the verge of resigning.

C2-10-0.note_es: El future perfect continuous mide la duración hasta un punto futuro; be to y be due to, planes oficiales; be on the verge of, algo inminente.

C2-10-1.point: Comparative structures with nuance (the more…the more, nowhere near, every bit as)
C2-10-1.title: How equal are the two things?

marks.ex: It’s nowhere near as big as ours.
It’s not quite as fast as mine.
She is every bit as skilled as he is.

C2-10-1.note_es: Estas estructuras miden la diferencia con precisión: de nowhere near as (mucho menos) a every bit as (exactamente igual).

C2-10-2.point: Proverbs, fixed expressions and register at C2
C2-10-2.title: Fixed expressions and register

items.t: In the light of these findings…

C2-10-2.note_es: Una expresión fija arrastra un registro: úsala solo donde encaja. A piece of cake es informal; it remains to be seen es formal.
